harness.note: Every claim was prototyped at this identical HEAD, one scratch worktree per claim, per ADR-013.

verification_method: Every gate was re-run by the supervisor against the worktree on disk. No claim is recorded on the strength of a session's own summary — that is the discarded self-report the project exists to refuse.

supervisor_found_defect.found: The claim-5 suite was reported stable and was not. Supervisor measured 2 failures in 16 full-suite runs (~12%), always NEGATIVE CONTROL, always expect(results.every(r => r.code === 0)).toBe(true) — a worker subprocess exit code, not a fencing assertion.
supervisor_found_defect.root_cause: worker.ts set PRAGMA busy_timeout AFTER PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL. The WAL mode change needs a brief exclusive lock and busy_timeout was still 0, so two concurrently-opening workers collided with SQLiteError: database is locked. The throw ran at module top level, outside the .catch() attached to Effect.runPromise, so it escaped unhandled and exited non-zero.
supervisor_found_defect.why_it_was_invisible: spawnWorker captured each worker's stderr and then discarded it — never asserted, never printed. The failure carried no signal, so repeated runs read as stable. Both reviewers approved, and DeepSeek's own re-runs likely hit the same race without recognising it.
supervisor_found_defect.isolated_proof: Minimal two-process repro of the same pragma sequence, run outside the worktree: current order 4/40 non-zero with 'SQLiteError: database is locked'; busy_timeout first 0/40.
supervisor_found_defect.fix: busy_timeout set first; journal_mode and DDL dropped from the worker (prepareDb owns them, WAL is persistent); DB setup wrapped in try/catch with deliberate non-zero exit; every scenario now inlines captured worker stderr on failure.
supervisor_found_defect.confirmed: Supervisor re-ran the full suite 20 consecutive times after the fix: 20/20 clean.
supervisor_found_defect.lesson: An unstable negative control is worse than an unstable test: the control's job is to show the defect returns when the fence is off, so a flaky control cannot distinguish a flake from a changed mechanism. Stability must be measured by repeated FULL-suite runs — isolated scenarios never spawn concurrently and never expose the race.

claims.title: Provider watchdog: idle + absolute timeout around llm.stream

embedded.scope: SLICE-011 claim 1 only (provider watchdog). Disposable prototype; ships nothing.
embedded.claimTitle: Provider watchdog: inactivity (idle) + absolute timeout around llm.stream
embedded.adr: ADR-015 (proposed 2026-08-06), Decision Outcome (1) and sad-path #1/#11; quality attribute 'Reliability: a provider stalls mid-stream -> run reaches a terminal state within budget'.

artifacts.change: +40/-4; idle guard via Stream.timeoutOrElse (~L236-251), absolute guard via Effect.raceFirst vs failing sleep (~L298-318), ProviderWatchdogConfig off-by-default (~L44-49). RunError union unchanged; both failures typed LLMError.

embedded.defect: A stalled provider stream (one chunk then silence) makes llm.stream(request).pipe(Stream.runForEach(...)) block forever, so the run never reaches a terminal state. Baseline proven by the existing manually-interrupted test verifyPartialFlushOnInterruption (session-runner.test.ts:525).

design.idle: Stream.timeoutOrElse({ duration: idle, orElse: () => Stream.fail(LLMError 'Provider stream idle timeout') }) wrapping llm.stream(request). Per-pull deadline that RESETS on every emitted chunk (verified in installed effect@4.0.0-beta.83 dist/Stream.js:2075-2109).
design.absolute: Effect.raceFirst(restore(providerStream), Effect.sleep(absolute).pipe(Effect.andThen(Effect.fail(LLMError 'Provider turn absolute timeout')))) inside the existing Effect.uninterruptibleMask. On budget elapse the blocked consumer is interrupted (raceAllFirst -> fiberInterruptAll, verified dist/internal/effect.js:948-975).
design.whyNotEffectTimeout: Effect.timeout widens the error type to Cause.TimeoutError, which is outside the RunError/LLMError union and would not satisfy `failure instanceof LLMError`. Both watchdog failures are kept as LLMError so existing failure-handling maps them to a terminal assistant-error state.
design.toggle: ProviderWatchdogConfig (module-level, OFF by default) so existing behavior is byte-identical when idle/absolute are undefined.

fixtures.slowComplete: Stream.fromIterable([stepStart, textStart, textDelta('Complete'), textEnd, stepFinish, finish]).pipe(Stream.tap(() => Effect.sleep('150 millis')))

claims.title: Reconciler reorder: hoist interrupted-tool reconciliation above the eligible-input guard

embedded.scope: SLICE-011 claim 2 only (reconciler reorder). Disposable prototype; ships nothing.
embedded.claimTitle: Reconciler reorder: hoist interrupted-tool reconciliation above the eligible-input guard + startup sweep
embedded.adr: ADR-015 (proposed 2026-08-06), Decision Outcome (2) and sad-path #2/#8; quality attribute 'Reliability: crash with an empty inbox -> stranded running tools reconciled at startup'.

artifacts.change: +13/-1; hoist yield* failInterruptedTools(sessionID) above the eligible-input guard (now ~L387-391, was after the ~L389 return); add reconcile = Effect.fn('SessionRunner.reconcile') calling failInterruptedTools, exposed on Service.of alongside run (~L411-415).
+2/-0; Interface gains readonly reconcile: (sessionID) => Effect.Effect<void, RunError> (startup-sweep capability).

embedded.defect: The reconciler returned on the eligible-input guard (runner/llm.ts:389, `if (!input.force && !hasSteer && !hasQueue) return`) BEFORE interrupted-tool reconciliation at :390 (`yield* failInterruptedTools(input.sessionID)`). A crash with an EMPTY inbox leaves a tool projected `running` forever: the empty inbox trips the guard's early return, so failInterruptedTools never runs. A crash with a pending steer would NOT trigger the bug (the guard passes) -> the empty-inbox path is the whole point (SLICE-011 decoration warning #2).

design.hoist: Move `yield* failInterruptedTools(input.sessionID)` to the first statement of run(), above the hasSteer/hasQueue reads and the eligible-input guard. failInterruptedTools iterates the session's projected context (store.context) and publishes a Tool.Failed event for every tool still `pending`/`running`; it is a no-op when none exist, so the normal drain flow is byte-identical when there are no stranded tools.
design.startupSweep: New SessionRunner.reconcile(sessionID) calls failInterruptedTools without scheduling a provider turn. Production wires this over all sessions at process start so a crash with an empty inbox (where nobody calls run()) is still recovered. The capability is added and tested here; automatic invocation over all sessions at boot is deferred to SLICE-012+.
design.idempotency: failInterruptedTools only acts on pending/running tools; after one pass the tool is `error`, so subsequent passes skip it. The projector's own Tool.Failed handler (message-updater.ts:323) re-checks `status === 'pending' || 'running'`, so projection is idempotent even under a duplicate event.

fixtures.strandedTool: Two-graph file-DB fixture. Graph 1 emits the durable events a provider turn leaves behind when the process is killed AFTER a tool is called but BEFORE it settles: publisher.publish(toolInputStart), toolInputEnd, toolCall({ id: 'call-stranded', name: 'echo', input }) with NO Tool.Success/Tool.Failed. The projector writes an assistant message with one tool projected `running`. The scope is torn down. This faithfully reproduces the post-SIGKILL durable state (the runner's own interruption path cannot strand a tool because runTurnAttempt is wrapped in Effect.uninterruptibleMask which reconciles on interrupt).
fixtures.twoGraph: Graph 2 reopens the same file-backed SQLite DB; the projected assistant message survived teardown as `running`. The inbox is asserted empty for BOTH steer and queue (SessionInput.hasPending) before the reconciler runs.

RED.setup: fix reverted (only the hoist removed; reconcile capability retained)

GREEN.meaning: hoist makes run() reconcile on the empty-inbox path; reconcile() marks the stranded tool interrupted without scheduling a provider turn.

The hoist adds exactly one failInterruptedTools call per run(); since it is a no-op with no stranded tools, all existing turns are byte-identical.

claims.title: Durable retry: attempt state survives a restart during the retry delay

embedded.scope: SLICE-011 claim 3 only (durable retry). Disposable prototype; ships nothing.
embedded.claimTitle: Durable retry: publish session.next.retried + project it so a fresh graph resumes from the persisted attempt count and next_attempt_at instead of resetting
embedded.adr: ADR-015 (proposed 2026-08-06), Decision Outcome (3), Considered Options 2 (rejected) and 5 (chosen), Improvement 4, sad-paths #3 (crash during retry delay) and #10 (retried projection double-fires); quality attribute 'Recoverability: process dies during retry delay -> next_attempt_at honoured; no early retry'.
embedded.architecturalReality: Uncommenting the projector alone persists NOTHING. The commented projector at projector.ts:394 routed to run(db, event) -> SessionMessageUpdater, which treats session.next.retried as a no-op (message-updater.ts:374 -> () => Effect.void). No attempt/next_attempt_at column or retry table existed anywhere in the schema (SessionTable in session/sql.ts had no retry fields; database/schema.gen.ts had none). The retry itself was process-local recursive state wholly below the session layer in packages/llm/src/route/executor.ts retryStatusFailures (executor.ts:345-364, installed at :378), invisible to the runner: the runner sees a retryable LLMError only AFTER the executor exhausts its retries (runner/llm.ts:317). So durable retry required (a) surfacing retry to the session layer, (b) making the projector write real state, and (c) teaching the drain to honour it before re-admitting.

artifacts.change: +115/-... : session-layer retry. RetryTurnError defect (L183) raised at end of runTurnAttempt on a retryable, pre-assistant-start, non-interrupted failure with attempt < MAX_RETRIES (retryFailure L320, die L381). runTurn and runAfterOverflowCompaction catch RetryTurnError via shared retryTurn() helper -> publish SessionEvent.Retried, Effect.sleep(retryDelay(attempt)), recurse attempt+1 (L422, L438). run() reads persisted retry_attempt/retry_next_attempt_at and Effect.sleeps until next_attempt_at BEFORE re-admitting (L461-470), bypasses the eligible-input guard when a retry is pending (L474), resumes attempt = retryAttempt+1 (L478), and clears retry state on settle. Constants 500/10000/2 re-declared local to the runner.

L394 uncommented and replaced: on SessionEvent.Retried, db.update(SessionTable).set({retry_attempt: event.data.attempt, retry_next_attempt_at: toEpochMillis(timestamp) + min(500*2^attempt, 10000)}) where id=sessionID. Mirrors the existing RevertEvent.Staged projector pattern (projector.ts:396-414). The old no-op run(db, event) path is NOT used.
L57-58: two nullable columns added to SessionTable: retry_attempt integer(), retry_next_attempt_at integer().

L366 makeLayer(retry) factory; L384 export const layer = makeLayer(true) (retry ON, unchanged behavior for all existing callers); L385 export const singleAttemptLayer = makeLayer(false). singleAttemptLayer is referenced nowhere outside its own definition; the global platform node (app-node-platform.ts) still uses RequestExecutor.layer, so non-session callers keep executor retry. The session path receives the LLMError on the first 503 so the session-layer retry owns durability.
Regenerated baseline to include the two new session columns.
Generated Drizzle migration adding retry_attempt and retry_next_attempt_at to the session table.

embedded.defect: Retry is process-local recursive state in packages/llm/src/route/executor.ts retryStatusFailures (Effect.catchTag -> Effect.sleep -> recurse with retries-1/attempt+1). If the process/graph is torn down during Effect.sleep, the attempt counter is lost; a fresh graph starts a new request at attempt 0. Every restart defeats a rate limit. ADR-015 driver: 'Retry state must survive restart'.

design.surfaceRetry: Retry is moved to the session layer. runTurnAttempt detects a retryable LLMError (status 429/503/504/529 via isRetryableStatus, mirroring executor retryableStatus) when attempt < MAX_RETRIES and the assistant has not started, and dies with a RetryTurnError defect (L381). runTurn/runAfterOverflowCompaction catch it via retryTurn(): publish SessionEvent.Retried {attempt, error:{message,statusCode,isRetryable:true}}, Effect.sleep(retryDelay(attempt)), recurse runTurn(attempt+1).
design.persist: The Retried projector (projector.ts:394) materializes attempt + next_attempt_at (= timestamp + min(500*2^attempt, 10000)) onto SessionTable. The durable session.next.retried event remains the source of truth; the columns are a materialized read model in the same shape as every other projector here (mirrors RevertEvent.Staged).
design.resume: run() (runner/llm.ts) reads retry_attempt/retry_next_attempt_at BEFORE the eligible-input guard. If a retry is pending and next_attempt_at is in the future it Effect.sleeps until then (L461-470) - it does NOT re-admit/call the provider during the delay. It resumes at attempt = retryAttempt+1 (L478). clearRetry() nulls both columns on turn settle (success or typed terminal failure).
design.executorNotDoubleRetry: singleAttemptLayer is exported for future production wiring of the session LLM client; it is NOT wired globally (P2a fix). The prototype test fakes LLMClient.Service directly so the executor is bypassed in the suite; the session-layer retry is what is proven.
design.backoff: Deterministic mid-point of executor retryDelay: min(500 * 2^attempt, 10000), no jitter, so the projector and the runner share one formula and TestClock timing is exact.

claims.title: Durable blockers: permission/question waits survive graph teardown

embedded.claim: ADR-015 claim 4 / SLICE-011 done-criterion 5 — durable blockers (sad paths 5 and 6)
embedded.thesis: Pending permission/question blockers are an in-memory Map cleared on location-layer teardown. Persist them as SQLite rows so the SAME blocker ID survives teardown, accepts EXACTLY ONE reply, and never re-runs the creating tool's pre-permission work.
embedded.anti_decoration_rule: The Deferred is NOT durable; the SQLite row is. Exactly-once is enforced by ROW DELETION on reply/reject. Persisting the payload and replaying into a fresh Deferred is decoration unless the same blocker ID accepts exactly one reply after teardown.

embedded.mode: disposable prototype (scratch suite, no commits, no pushes)
embedded.thesis_under_test: Ownership is an in-memory Map (packages/core/src/session/run-coordinator.ts:28) over a globally shared SQLite DB (packages/core/src/database/database.ts:53). Two live processes can therefore double-drain one Session. The fence is the existing effect-flock (packages/core/src/util/effect-flock.ts) keyed on sessionID plus EventSequenceTable.owner_id claim/refuse (packages/core/src/event.ts:254,274,291,525; schema packages/core/src/database/schema.gen.ts:73-77).

stability_history.symptom: 2 failures in 16 full-suite runs (~12%), always NEGATIVE CONTROL at the `expect(results.every(r=>r.code===0)).toBe(true)` line — a worker subprocess exited non-zero. Every fencing assertion still passed, so the failure carried no fencing signal.
stability_history.root_cause: FIXTURE BUG, not a fencing bug. worker.ts set PRAGMA busy_timeout AFTER PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL; the journal_mode change needs a brief exclusive lock and busy_timeout was still 0, so two workers opening the shared DB concurrently collided with SQLiteError 'database is locked'. The throw ran at module top level, OUTSIDE the Effect.runPromise .catch(), so it escaped unhandled. GREEN escaped only because its startAfterFile handshake serializes startup.
stability_history.why_it_read_as_stable: spawnWorker collected worker stderr and then discarded it; the failure was diagnostically blank.
stability_history.fix: (1) worker.ts: busy_timeout is now the first pragma; journal_mode and the DDL were dropped entirely (prepareDb in the orchestrator already creates the DB in WAL with the schema, and WAL is persistent). (2) worker.ts: DB setup is wrapped in try/catch that writes a clear stderr and exits non-zero deliberately. (3) ownership-fence.test.ts: every scenario calls assertWorkersOk, which throws with the captured worker stderr inlined on any non-zero exit. (4) re-measured: 20/20 full-suite runs green.
stability_history.lesson: a control that is itself flaky cannot distinguish a startup race from a changed mechanism — the negative control's stability is load-bearing evidence.
